consensus_summary: Mainstream consensus holds that 'holy' (qadosh/hagios) primarily means set apart/separated/consecrated for God and thus distinct from the common or profane, with closely linked senses of divine transcendence/otherness (when predicated of God) and moral purity or cultic status (when predicated of people, places, objects).
book_summary: Set apart from the common; for created things, claimed by God for an appointed purpose.
consensus_core_identification: set apart / consecrated / belonging to God and distinct from the common or profane
book_core_identification: set apart from the common (for created things: claimed by God for an appointed purpose)
boundary_disagreement: None material; book simply foregrounds the 'created things' application without excluding the consensus range.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both identify holiness first as separation from the common unto God. Consensus secondary strands (moral purity, numinous otherness, cultic status) are applications or consequences of that same core, not rival referents; the book's brief gloss and its printed texts stay inside that core without replacement or boundary shift.
strongest_objection: The entry is silent on God's own holiness and on moral-purity connotations that many consensus sources treat as tightly connected.
